translations.idiomatic: Preface

sentences.zh: 昔八卦兆而天人之理著，九疇序而帝王之應明。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Eight Trigrams appeared as omens and the principle of Heaven and man was made manifest; the Nine Categories were ordered and the responses of emperors and kings were clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when the Eight Trigrams first appeared as portents, the correspondence between Heaven and man became clear; once the Nine Categories were set in order, the way sovereigns answered to cosmic signs was likewise plain.

sentences.zh: 雖可以知從德獲自天之祐，違道陷神聽之罪，然未詳舉徵效，備考幽明，雖時列鼎雉庭穀之異，然而未究者眾矣。

translations.literal: Although one may know that following virtue wins blessing from Heaven and violating the Way incurs the crime of offending divine hearing, yet signs and effects were not fully enumerated nor the hidden and manifest thoroughly examined; although at times wonders such as tripods, pheasants, and grain in the courtyard were listed, still what had not been investigated remained numerous.
translations.idiomatic: One could already see that virtue brings Heaven's favor and transgression invites divine judgment, yet the records still lacked full catalogues of portents and proofs linking the unseen to the visible. Striking omens—tripods, pheasants, grain sprouting in the court—were sometimes noted, but vast stretches of such phenomena went unexplained.

sentences.zh: 至於鑑悟後王，多有所闕。

translations.literal: As for discerning and enlightening later kings, much was still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to instructing later rulers, the existing accounts left much to be desired.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼作春秋，具書祥眚，以驗行事。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, fully recording auspicious signs and calamities to verify conduct in government.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, recording omens and disasters in full so that deeds in government might be tested against them.

sentences.zh: 是則九疇陳其義於前，春秋列其效於後也。

translations.literal: Thus the Nine Categories set forth their meaning beforehand, and the Spring and Autumn listed their effects afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Categories laid out the theory in advance; the Spring and Autumn then displayed how those principles worked out in events.

sentences.zh: 逮至伏生創紀大傳，五行之體始詳；

translations.literal: Down to Fu Sheng, who created the Great Tradition, the substance of the Five Elements first became detailed;
translations.idiomatic: By the time Fu Sheng compiled the Great Tradition, the framework of the Five Elements had finally been spelled out in detail.

sentences.zh: 劉向廣演洪範，休咎之文益備。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang broadly expounded the Hong Fan, and the texts on fortune and misfortune grew ever more complete.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang developed the Hong Fan at length, so that writings on blessing and calamity became increasingly thorough.

sentences.zh: 故班固斟酌經、傳，詳紀條流，誠以一王之典，不可獨闕故也。

translations.literal: Therefore Ban Gu weighed the classics and commentaries and recorded the categories in detail—truly because the statutes of a single dynasty cannot properly omit this subject.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu therefore sifted the classics and their commentaries and set down the full sequence of categories, for the institutional record of any dynasty cannot rightly leave this matter out.

sentences.zh: 夫天道雖無聲無臭，然而應若影響，天人之驗，理不可誣。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven, though without sound or odor, nevertheless responds like shadow to form; the verification of Heaven and man cannot be deceived by reason.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way is silent and scentless, yet it answers events as a shadow answers a body; the correspondence between Heaven and humanity is a principle that reason cannot deny.

sentences.zh: 司馬彪纂集光武以來，以究漢事；

translations.literal: Sima Biao gathered materials from Emperor Guangwu onward to investigate Han affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao collected records from the reign of Emperor Guangwu onward in order to examine Han history.

sentences.zh: 王沈魏書志篇闕，凡厥災異，但編帝紀而已。

translations.literal: Wang Shen's Book of Wei lacked treatise chapters; all such disasters and anomalies were merely entered in the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: In Wang Shen's Book of Wei the treatise sections were missing, so every disaster and prodigy was relegated to the imperial annals alone.

sentences.zh: 自黃初以降，二百餘年，覽其災妖，以考之事，常若重規沓矩，不謬前說。

translations.literal: From the Huangchu era down, for more than two hundred years, surveying their disasters and portents to examine events, it was constantly as if one compass overlay another—never at odds with earlier explanations.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huangchu reign onward, across more than two hundred years, a review of disasters and portents against the events they accompanied shows the pattern repeating like one ruler laid upon another, never contradicting earlier doctrine.

sentences.zh: 又高堂隆、郭景純等，據經立辭，終皆顯應。

translations.literal: Moreover Gao Tanglong, Guo Jingchun, and others, grounding their words in the classics, in the end all met with manifest fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong, Guo Jingchun, and others likewise argued from the classics, and in the end their warnings all proved visibly true.

sentences.zh: 闕而不序，史體將虧。

translations.literal: To omit them and leave them unordered would impair the historiographical form.
translations.idiomatic: To leave such material out and untreatised would cripple the proper form of history writing.

sentences.zh: 今自司馬彪以後，皆撰次論序，斯亦班固遠采春秋，舉遠明近之例也。

translations.literal: Now from Sima Biao onward all are arranged and discussed in sequence—this too is Ban Gu's example of drawing from the distant Spring and Autumn to illuminate the near.
translations.idiomatic: From Sima Biao onward everything is arranged and discussed in order—following Ban Gu's precedent of taking the remote Spring and Autumn as a model to clarify the recent past.

sentences.zh: 又按言之不從，有介蟲之孽，劉歆以為毛蟲；

translations.literal: Moreover, according to "speech not heeded," there is the bane of shelled creatures; Liu Xin held that these were hairy creatures;
translations.idiomatic: Again, where "speech goes unheeded," the omen is shelled creatures; Liu Xin classified these as hairy creatures.

sentences.zh: 視之不明，有蠃蟲之孽，劉歆以為羽蟲。

translations.literal: according to "vision not clear," there is the bane of naked creatures; Liu Xin held that these were feathered creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Where "vision is unclear," the omen is naked creatures; Liu Xin classified these as feathered creatures.

sentences.zh: 按月令，夏蟲羽，秋蟲毛，宜如歆說，是以舊史從之。

translations.literal: According to the Monthly Ordinances, summer insects are feathered and autumn insects are hairy; Xin's view is fitting, and therefore the old histories follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances say that summer insects are feathered and autumn insects hairy, which supports Xin's view; the older histories therefore follow him.

sentences.zh: 五行精微，非末學所究。

translations.literal: The subtleties of the Five Elements are not for shallow learning to exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: The fine points of the Five Elements lie beyond what superficial scholarship can master.

sentences.zh: 凡已經前議者，並即其言以釋之；

translations.literal: Where there has already been prior discussion, I adopt those words in explanation;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever earlier scholars have already spoken on a point, I explain it in their terms.

sentences.zh: 未有舊說者，推準事理，以俟來哲。

translations.literal: where there is no old interpretation, I infer by reason and event, awaiting later sages.
translations.idiomatic: Where no earlier interpretation exists, I reason from principle and circumstance and leave the matter for wiser men to come.

sentences.zh: 五行傳曰：「田獵不宿，飲食不享，出入不節，奪民農時，及有姦謀，則木不曲直，謂木失其性而為災也。

translations.literal: The Tradition of the Five Elements says: "If one hunts without lodging overnight, does not offer food and drink, is immoderate in coming and going, robs the people of farming seasons, or engages in treacherous plots, then wood will not be straight or bent"—meaning wood loses its nature and becomes a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of the Five Elements states: "When the ruler hunts without staying the night, fails to present offerings at meals, is unrestrained in comings and goings, steals the people's farming seasons, or harbors treacherous designs, wood loses its power to be straight or bent"—that is, wood abandons its proper nature and disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅。

translations.literal: " It also says: "When appearance is not respectful, this is called lack of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: " It further says: "When deportment lacks respect, this is called irreverence.

sentences.zh: 厥咎狂，厥罰恒雨，厥極惡。

translations.literal: Its fault is madness, its punishment unending rain, its extreme evil.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is frenzy, the punishment incessant rain, the extreme outcome ruin.

sentences.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，時則有雞禍，時則有下體生上之痾，時則有青眚、青祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are strange garments, at such times tortoise portents, at such times chicken calamities, at such times the malady of the lower body growing upon the upper, at such times blue calamities and blue omens.
translations.idiomatic: Then come outlandish dress, tortoise prodigies, chicken disasters, the deformity of lower parts sprouting above, and blue calamities and blue portents.

sentences.zh: 惟金沴木。

translations.literal: Only metal harms wood.
translations.idiomatic: It is metal violating wood.

sentences.zh: 」班固曰：「蓋工匠為輪矢者多傷敗，及木為變怪。

translations.literal: " Ban Gu says: "Generally when craftsmen make wheels and arrows many are damaged, and when wood becomes strange transformations.
translations.idiomatic: " Ban Gu says: "Craftsmen making wheels and arrows often ruin their work, and wood itself turns into uncanny shapes.

sentences.zh: 」皆為不曲直也。

translations.literal: " All are cases of not being straight or bent.
translations.idiomatic: " All these are instances of wood failing to be straight or bent.

sentences.zh: 木不曲直

translations.literal: Wood not straight or bent
translations.idiomatic: Wood Fails to Be Straight or Bent

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初六年正月，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Huangchu of Emperor Wen of Wei, it rained and trees were coated with ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei's reign, rain fell and ice formed on the trees.

sentences.zh: 接劉歆說，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: Following Liu Xin's explanation, this is wood not straight or bent.
translations.idiomatic: Following Liu Xin's interpretation, this is a case of wood failing to be straight or bent.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「冰者陰之盛，木者少陽，貴臣象也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: "Ice is the fullness of yin; wood is lesser yang, the image of honored ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said: "Ice represents the dominance of yin; wood represents lesser yang and symbolizes high ministers.

sentences.zh: 此人將有害，則陰氣脅木，木先寒，故得雨而冰也。

translations.literal: When such a person is about to do harm, yin qi oppresses wood; wood grows cold first, and therefore receives rain and turns to ice.
translations.idiomatic: When such a man is about to bring harm, yin force presses upon wood; the wood chills first, and so rain turns to ice upon it.

sentences.zh: 」是年六月，利成郡兵蔡方等殺太守徐質，據郡反，多所脅略，并聚亡命。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month of that year, the soldier Cai Fang of Licheng commandery and others killed the prefect Xu Zhi, seized the commandery in rebellion, coerced many into following them, and gathered fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month of that year, Cai Fang and other troops of Licheng commandery killed Prefect Xu Zhi, rebelled and held the commandery, forced many into their service, and rallied fugitives.

sentences.zh: 遣二校尉與青州刺史共討平之。

translations.literal: Two commandants were sent with the Inspector of Qing Province jointly to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched two commandants, who together with the Inspector of Qing Province put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 太守，古之諸侯，貴臣有害之應也。

translations.literal: The prefect was the ancient feudal lord; this was the response to harm befalling honored ministers.
translations.idiomatic: A prefect corresponded to the feudal lords of old; the killing of such a minister was the fulfillment of the omen.

sentences.zh: 一說以木冰為甲兵之象。

translations.literal: One interpretation holds that ice on wood is the image of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Another view takes ice on wood as a sign of arms and warfare.

sentences.zh: 是歲，既討蔡方，又八月，天子自將以舟師征吳，戎卒十餘萬，連旍數百里，臨江觀兵。

translations.literal: That year, after Cai Fang had been suppressed, in the eighth month the Son of Heaven personally led a fleet against Wu; more than a hundred thousand soldiers marched, their banners stretching for hundreds of li as he reviewed the troops along the river.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, once Cai Fang had been crushed, the emperor in the eighth month led a naval expedition against Wu in person; over a hundred thousand troops advanced, their banners lining the riverbank for hundreds of li as he inspected the army.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興三年二月辛未，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the second month of the third year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, it rained and trees were coated with ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the second month of the third year of Taixing, Emperor Yuan of Jin's reign, rain fell and ice formed on the trees.

sentences.zh: 後二年，周顗、戴淵、刁協、劉隗皆遇害，與春秋同事，是其應也。

translations.literal: Two years later Zhou Yi, Dai Yuan, Diao Xie, and Liu Wei were all killed; it was the same matter as in the Spring and Autumn Annals—this was the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Zhou Yi, Dai Yuan, Diao Xie, and Liu Wei all met violent deaths—the same pattern recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the omen's fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 一曰，是後王敦攻京師，又其象也。

translations.literal: One account says that afterward Wang Dun attacked the capital—this too was its sign.
translations.idiomatic: Another account says that afterward Wang Dun attacked the capital—that too was foreshadowed.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和八年正月乙巳，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the first month of the eighth year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, it rained and trees were coated with ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the first month of the eighth year of Yonghe, Emperor Mu of Jin's reign, rain fell and ice formed on the trees.

sentences.zh: 是年，殷浩北伐，明年，軍敗，十年，廢黜。

translations.literal: That year Yin Hao launched a northern campaign; the next year the army was defeated, and in the tenth year he was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yin Hao marched north; the next year his army was routed, and in the tenth year he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 又曰，荀羨、殷浩北伐，桓溫入關之象也。

translations.literal: Another account says this foreshadowed Xun Xian and Yin Hao's northern campaigns and Huan Wen's entry into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Another reading says it foreshadowed the northern expeditions of Xun Xian and Yin Hao and Huan Wen's advance into the passes.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十四年十二月乙巳，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, it rained and trees were coated with ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu of Jin's reign, rain fell and ice formed on the trees.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，王恭為北蕃；

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Wang Gong became defender of the northern frontier;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the next year Wang Gong was posted to the northern frontier;

sentences.zh: 八月，庾楷為西蕃；

translations.literal: in the eighth month Yu Kai became defender of the western frontier;
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month Yu Kai took the western frontier;

sentences.zh: 九月，王國寶為中書令，尋加領軍將軍；

translations.literal: in the ninth month Wang Guobao became Director of the Secretariat, and soon afterward was also made General Who Leads the Army;
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month Wang Guobao was appointed Director of the Secretariat and shortly thereafter made General Who Leads the Army;

sentences.zh: 十七年殷仲堪為荊州。

translations.literal: in the seventeenth year Yin Zhongkan became Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: in the seventeenth year Yin Zhongkan became Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 雖邪正異規，而終同摧滅，是其應也。

translations.literal: Although the wicked and the upright followed different courses, in the end all were alike destroyed—this was the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Though loyalists and schemers pursued different paths, all were ultimately swept away—the omen's fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 一曰，苻堅雖敗，關、河未一，丁零鮮卑，侵略司、兗，竇揚勝扇逼梁、雍，兵役不已，又其象也。

translations.literal: One account says that although Fu Jian had been defeated, the passes and rivers were not yet united; the Dingling and Xianbei raided Si and Yan provinces; Dou Yang and Yang Sheng stirred up trouble in Liang and Yong; military service never ceased—this too was its sign.
translations.idiomatic: One account adds that even after Fu Jian's defeat the heartland remained divided, Dingling and Xianbei bands harried Si and Yan, Dou Yang and Yang Sheng stirred rebellion in Liang and Yong, and levies never ended—signs of the same kind.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮建興二年，諸葛恪征淮南，行後，所坐聽事棟中折。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianxing of Sun Liang of Wu, when Zhuge Ke campaigned against Huainan, after he had set out the central beam of the hall in which he sat broke.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianxing, Sun Liang of Wu's reign, Zhuge Ke marched against Huainan; after he departed, the main beam of his audience hall snapped.

sentences.zh: 恪妄興徵役，奪民農時，作為邪謀，傷國財力，故木失其性，致毀折也。

translations.literal: Ke wantonly raised levies, robbed the people of farming seasons, engaged in perverse plots, and injured the state's wealth and strength; therefore wood lost its nature and suffered breakage.
translations.idiomatic: Ke had recklessly imposed corvée, stolen the farming season, pursued treacherous designs, and drained the treasury; wood therefore lost its nature and the beam broke.

sentences.zh: 及旋師而誅滅，於周易又為棟橈之凶也。

translations.literal: When he returned and was executed, in the Book of Changes this was again the misfortune of "a bent ridgepole."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was put to death—the Book of Changes calls such a fate "the ridgepole bent to breaking."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康五年五月，宣帝廟地陷梁折。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, the ground of Emperor Xuan's temple sank and a beam broke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Taikang, Emperor Wu of Jin's reign, the ground of Emperor Xuan's temple subsided and a beam snapped.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，太廟殿又陷，改作廟，築基及泉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the Grand Temple hall sank again; the temple was rebuilt and the foundation driven down to the spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year the Grand Temple hall collapsed again; the temple was rebuilt and the foundations dug until they reached groundwater.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，遂更營新廟，遠致名材，雜以銅柱。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year a new temple was then built, famous timber brought from afar and mixed with bronze pillars.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month work began on a new temple, with prized timber fetched from distant regions and bronze pillars set among the timbers.

sentences.zh: 陳勰為匠，作者六萬人。

translations.literal: Chen Shao served as master craftsman, and the laborers numbered sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shao directed the construction, and sixty thousand workers were employed.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，乃成。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚寅，梁又折。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the eleventh month a beam broke again.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the eleventh month another beam snapped.

sentences.zh: 按地陷者，分離之象，梁折者，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: Ground sinking is the image of separation; beam breaking is wood not straight or bent.
translations.idiomatic: Where the ground sinks, the sign is separation; where beams break, wood has failed to be straight or bent.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：于時後宮殿有孽火，又廟梁無故自折。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: At that time there was uncanny fire in the rear palaces, and temple beams broke for no apparent reason.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng wrote: About then uncanny fires broke out in the rear palaces, and temple beams snapped without cause.

sentences.zh: 先是帝多不豫，益惡之。

translations.literal: Before this the emperor had often been unwell and grew all the more troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long been in poor health and took these signs as still worse omens.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝崩，而王室頻亂，遂亡天下。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died, the royal house fell into repeated turmoil, and the realm was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died; the house of Jin convulsed again and again until the dynasty was gone.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，成都王穎使陸機率眾向京師，擊長沙王乂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, sent Lu Ji at the head of an army toward the capital to attack the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tai'an, Emperor Hui of Jin's reign, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, ordered Lu Ji to march on the capital and strike the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.

sentences.zh: 軍始引而牙竿折，俄而戰敗，機被誅。

translations.literal: As soon as the army set out the command pennant staff snapped; soon afterward they were defeated and Ji was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The army had barely moved when the command pennant pole broke; shortly afterward the force was routed and Lu Ji was put to death.

sentences.zh: 穎尋奔潰，卒賜死。

translations.literal: Ying soon fled in rout and in the end was ordered to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Ying soon fled in defeat and was eventually compelled to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 初，河間王顒謀先誅長沙，廢太子，立穎。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had plotted first to kill the Prince of Changsha, depose the heir, and install Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had planned to kill the Prince of Changsha first, depose the crown prince, and set up Ying in his place.

sentences.zh: 長沙知之，誅其黨卞粹等，故穎來伐。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha learned of it and executed his partisans Bian Cui and others; therefore Ying came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changsha uncovered the plot and executed Yong's allies Bian Cui and the rest, which brought Ying's invasion.

sentences.zh: 機又以穎得遐邇心，將為漢之代王，遂委質於穎，為犯從之將。

translations.literal: Ji also thought that because Ying had won the hearts of near and far he would become the Han dynasty's replacement king, and therefore submitted to Ying and served as a general who followed the rebel cause.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji likewise believed Ying had won universal support and would replace the Han house as king; he therefore pledged himself to Ying and served as a general in the rebel host.

sentences.zh: 此皆姦謀之罰，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: All these were punishments for treacherous plots—wood not straight or bent.
translations.idiomatic: All of this fell under the penalty for treacherous designs—wood failing to be straight or bent.

sentences.zh: 王敦在武昌，鈴下儀仗生華如蓮花狀，五六日而萎落。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun was at Wuchang, the ceremonial regalia under the bells sprouted blossoms like lotus flowers, which withered after five or six days.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Dun held Wuchang, the ceremonial gear beneath the bells put forth lotus-like blossoms that faded within five or six days.

sentences.zh: 此木失其性而為變也。

translations.literal: This was wood losing its nature and turning into a transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Wood had lost its proper nature and produced this uncanny change.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「鈴閤，尊貴者之儀；

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "The bell pavilion is the ceremonial of the honored;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "The bell pavilion houses the regalia of the great;

sentences.zh: 鈴下，主威儀之官。

translations.literal: those under the bells are officials who maintain majesty and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: the attendants beneath the bells are officers charged with upholding royal dignity.

sentences.zh: 今狂花生於枯木，又在鈴閤之間，言威儀之富，榮華之盛，皆如狂花之發，不可久也。

translations.literal: Now wild flowers grow on withered wood, and moreover within the bell pavilion—this means that the richness of majesty and the splendor of glory are all like the blooming of mad flowers and cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Wild blossoms now spring from dead wood inside the bell pavilion itself—a sign that pomp and glory flourish like freak blooms and cannot last.

sentences.zh: 」其後終以逆命，沒又加戮，是其應也。

translations.literal: " Afterward he ended in rebellion against his mandate; after death he suffered further punishment—this was the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he died in rebellion against his mandate and was disgraced even after death—the omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 一說此花孽也，於周易為「枯楊生華」。

translations.literal: One account says this flowering was a bane; in the Book of Changes it is "the withered poplar puts forth flowers."
translations.idiomatic: Another account calls the blossoms a portent of ruin; in the Book of Changes the image is "the withered poplar blooms."

sentences.zh: 桓玄始篡，龍旂竿折。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan first usurped power, the dragon-banner pole snapped.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan first seized power, the dragon-banner staff broke.

sentences.zh: 玄田獵出入，不絕昏夜，飲食恣奢，土水妨農，又多姦謀，故木失其性也。

translations.literal: Xuan hunted without cease day or night, indulged food and drink without restraint, let earthworks and waterworks hinder farming, and engaged in many treacherous plots; therefore wood lost its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan hunted day and night without pause, feasted without restraint, let irrigation works steal the farming season, and pursued endless treachery—wood therefore lost its nature.

sentences.zh: 夫旂所以擬三辰，章著明也。

translations.literal: Banners are meant to image the three luminaries and to display brightness manifestly.
translations.idiomatic: Banners image the three luminaries and proclaim radiance for all to see.

sentences.zh: 旂竿之折，高明去矣。

translations.literal: When the banner pole snaps, loftiness and brightness depart.
translations.idiomatic: When the pole snaps, height and clarity are gone.

sentences.zh: 在位八十日而敗。

translations.literal: He held power for eighty days and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled for eighty days and fell.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始二年五月丙午，南琅邪臨沂黃城山道士盛道度堂屋一柱自然，夜光照室內。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, at Huangcheng Mountain in Linyi, Nanlangya, a pillar in the hall of the Daoist Sheng Daodu of its own accord [glowed], and at night its light filled the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi, Emperor Ming of Song's reign, a hall pillar at Huangcheng Mountain in Linyi, Nanlangya, belonging to the Daoist priest Sheng Daodu glowed of itself, lighting the room through the night.

sentences.zh: 此木失其性也。

translations.literal: This was wood losing its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Wood had lost its proper nature.

sentences.zh: 或云木腐自光。

translations.literal: Some say rotting wood shines of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Some explain it as rotten timber emitting light on its own.

sentences.zh: 廢帝昇明元年，吳興餘杭舍亭禾蕈樹生李實。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming of the deposed emperor, at Sheting in Yuhang, Wuxing, a hawthorn growing on a straw-mushroom tree bore plum fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming, the deposed emperor's reign, at Sheting in Yuhang, Wuxing, a hawthorn grafted on a straw-mushroom tree produced plum fruit.

sentences.zh: 禾蕈樹，民間所謂胡頹樹。

translations.literal: The straw-mushroom tree is what common people call the "barbarian tumble" tree.
translations.idiomatic: The straw-mushroom tree is the species folk call the "barbarian tumble" tree.

sentences.zh: 貌不恭

translations.literal: Appearance not respectful
translations.idiomatic: Appearance Lacks Respect

sentences.zh: 魏文帝居諒闇之始，便數出遊獵體，貌不重，風尚通脫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's period of mourning seclusion he repeatedly went out hunting and sporting; his bearing was not grave and his fashion was unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: From the very start of his mourning seclusion Emperor Wen of Wei went out again and again to hunt and roam; he carried himself without gravity and set a fashion of license.

sentences.zh: 故戴凌以直諫抵罪，鮑勛以迕旨極刑。

translations.literal: Therefore Dai Ling was punished for blunt remonstrance and Bao Xun was executed for defying the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ling was punished for blunt remonstrance and Bao Xun was put to death for crossing the throne's will.

sentences.zh: 天下化之，咸賤守節，此貌之不恭也。

translations.literal: The realm took its cue from him and all came to despise steadfast integrity—this was appearance not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The empire followed his example and learned to scorn constancy—appearance lacking respect.

sentences.zh: 是以享國不永，後祚短促。

translations.literal: Therefore his enjoyment of the state was not long and his later fortune was brief.
translations.idiomatic: Hence his own reign did not last, and his line's fortune proved short.

sentences.zh: 春秋魯君居喪不哀，在慼而有嘉容，穆叔謂之不度，後終出奔。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals a lord of Lu in mourning was not sorrowful and in grief yet wore a pleasing countenance; Muzhong called this lack of measure, and in the end he fled into exile.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records a ruler of Lu who, while in mourning, showed no grief yet wore a pleasant face; Muzhong called this want of propriety, and the man ended in exile.

sentences.zh: 蓋同事也。

translations.literal: It is essentially the same matter.
translations.idiomatic: The cases are essentially the same.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書鄧颺，行步弛縱，筋不束體，坐起傾倚，若無手足。

translations.literal: Deng Yang of Wei, Director of the Secretariat, walked with loose stride, his sinews not binding his body; sitting or rising he leaned and slumped as if he had no hands or feet.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang, Director of the Secretariat under Wei, walked with a loose, sprawling gait, his sinews seeming not to hold his frame together; whether sitting or rising he lolled and leaned as though he lacked hands and feet.

sentences.zh: 此貌之不恭也。

translations.literal: This was appearance not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: This too was appearance lacking respect.

sentences.zh: 管輅謂之鬼躁。

translations.literal: Guan Luo called it "ghost frenzy."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Luo named it "demon restlessness."

sentences.zh: 鬼躁者，凶終之徵。

translations.literal: "Ghost frenzy" is the sign of a violent end.
translations.idiomatic: "Demon restlessness" foretells a violent death.

sentences.zh: 後卒誅死。

translations.literal: In the end he was executed and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually put to death.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，貴遊子弟相與為散髮倮身之飲，對弄婢妾。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, young nobles joined together in drinking parties with hair loose and bodies naked, sporting with maidservants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Hui of Jin's Yuankang era, scions of the elite held drinking parties with hair unbound and bodies bare, dallying with maids and concubines.

sentences.zh: 逆之者傷好，非之者負譏。

translations.literal: Those who resisted were wounded in their friendships; those who disapproved bore ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who refused was ostracized; anyone who criticized was mocked.

sentences.zh: 希世之士，恥不與焉。

translations.literal: Men who sought the fashion of the age were ashamed not to take part.
translations.idiomatic: Men who prided themselves on keeping up with the times were ashamed to stay away.

sentences.zh: 蓋胡、翟侵中國之萌也。

translations.literal: This was surely the sprouting of the Hu and Di invading the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: It was the first sign that the northern tribes would overrun the heartland.

sentences.zh: 豈徒伊川之民，一被髮而祭者乎。

translations.literal: Was it only the people of Yichuan who once let down their hair and offered sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Had it come to nothing more than the people of Yichuan letting down their hair for sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，賈謐親貴，數入二宮，與儲君遊戲，无降下心。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, Jia Mi enjoyed intimate favor and repeatedly entered the two palaces to play with the heir apparent, without a submissive heart.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang, Jia Mi, riding on intimate favor, entered the inner palaces again and again to sport with the crown prince and showed no deference.

sentences.zh: 又嘗同弈棊爭道，成都王穎厲色曰：「皇太子，國之儲貳。

translations.literal: Once when they played go and disputed the board, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, said sternly: "The crown prince is the state's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Once, disputing a game of go, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, said sharply: "The crown prince is the heir of the realm.

sentences.zh: 賈謐何敢無禮！

translations.literal: How dare Jia Mi be discourteous!
translations.idiomatic: How dare Jia Mi behave without courtesy!

sentences.zh: 」謐猶不悛，故及於禍。

translations.literal: " Mi still did not reform himself; therefore he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi still would not mend his ways, and so brought disaster on himself.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏既誅趙倫，因留輔政，坐拜百官，符敕臺府，淫醟專驕，不一朝覲。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, had executed Zhao Lun, he remained to assist in government, sat to receive the obeisance of all officials, issued orders in the name of the Secretariat, and was dissolute, arrogant, and exclusive—never once attending court audience.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Jiong of Qi had killed Zhao Lun he stayed on as regent, accepted officials' bows while seated, issued Secretariat orders at will, and grew drunken, arrogant, and aloof—never attending court.

sentences.zh: 此狂恣不肅之容也。

translations.literal: This was the bearing of mad presumption without reverence.
translations.idiomatic: This was the deportment of reckless insolence without respect.

sentences.zh: 天下莫不高其功，而慮其亡也。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm none failed to praise his achievement, yet all feared his ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The empire applauded his success yet dreaded his fall.

sentences.zh: 冏終弗改，遂至夷滅。

translations.literal: Jiong in the end did not change and proceeded to extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong never reformed and was destroyed in the end.

sentences.zh: 太元中，人不復著帩頭。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era people no longer wore the kerchief head-wrap.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan era people ceased to wear the kerchief that bound the head.

sentences.zh: 頭者，元首，帩者，令髮不垂，助元首為儀飾者也。

translations.literal: The head is the chief; the kerchief keeps the hair from hanging loose and assists the chief as ritual adornment.
translations.idiomatic: The head is the sovereign part of the body; the kerchief keeps the hair in place and helps complete the ritual appearance of the head.

sentences.zh: 今忽廢之，若人君獨立無輔，以至危亡也。

translations.literal: Now it was suddenly abandoned—as if the ruler stood alone without assistants, leading to danger and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: To cast it off suddenly was as if a ruler stood without ministers—an omen of peril and collapse.

sentences.zh: 其後桓玄篡位。

translations.literal: Afterward Huan Xuan usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huan Xuan seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 舊為屐者，齒皆達楄上，名曰「露卯」。

translations.literal: Formerly wooden clogs had teeth reaching the upper rim, called "exposed mortise."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly clogs were made with teeth reaching the upper frame, called "exposed mortise."

sentences.zh: 太元中，忽不徹，名曰「陰卯」。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era people suddenly stopped cutting them through, calling them "hidden mortise."
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan era people suddenly left the teeth uncut, calling them "hidden mortise."

sentences.zh: 其後多陰謀，遂致大亂。

translations.literal: Afterward there were many secret plots and great disorder followed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward secret intrigues multiplied until the realm fell into great chaos.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙七年，晉朝拜授劉毅世子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, the Jin court invested Liu Yi's heir by imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yixi, Emperor An of Jin's reign, the court bestowed investiture on Liu Yi's heir.

sentences.zh: 毅以王命之重，當設饗宴親，請吏佐臨視。

translations.literal: Yi held the king's command weighty and ought to have set out a feast for kin and asked his staff to attend in person.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi regarded the royal mandate as weighty and should have held a feast for his kin and asked his officers to witness it.

sentences.zh: 至日，國僚不重白，默拜於廄中。

translations.literal: When the day came, the state officials did not announce it again; they bowed in silence in the stable.
translations.idiomatic: On the day appointed the state staff failed to announce the ceremony and performed a silent obeisance in the stable.

sentences.zh: 王人將反命，毅方知，大以為恨，免郎中令劉敬叔官。

translations.literal: When the king's envoy was about to return with the report, Yi only then learned of it and was deeply resentful, removing Director of Gentlemen Liu Jingshu from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial envoy was about to report back, Yi learned what had happened, was deeply offended, and dismissed Director of Gentlemen Liu Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 識者怪焉。

translations.literal: Observers found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers regarded the affair as uncanny.

sentences.zh: 此墮略嘉禮，不肅之妖也。

translations.literal: This was the portent of neglecting and slighting fine ritual—improper conduct without reverence.
translations.idiomatic: This was the omen of scorning proper ceremony—conduct lacking reverence.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝靈運有逸才，每出入，自扶接者常數人。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun of Chen commandery had exceptional talent; whenever he went out or in, those who supported him numbered several men.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun of Chen commandery possessed outstanding talent; whenever he went abroad, several men steadied him.

sentences.zh: 民間謠曰「四人挈衣裙，三人捉坐席」是也。

translations.literal: The folk song says, "Four men hold his skirt and robe, three men seize his mat and seat"—this is the case.
translations.idiomatic: A popular rhyme runs, "Four men hold skirt and robe, three men seize mat and seat"—exactly this.

sentences.zh: 此蓋不肅之咎，後坐誅。

translations.literal: This was the fault of irreverence; afterward he was executed for it.
translations.idiomatic: This too was irreverence; he was later executed.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始中，幸臣阮佃夫勢傾朝廷，室宇豪麗，車服鮮明，乘車常偏向一邊，違正立執綏之體。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Emperor Ming of Song, the favorite Ruan Tianfu's power bent the court; his dwellings were sumptuous, his carriage and dress brilliant; when he rode his carriage often leaned to one side, violating the upright posture of grasping the reins.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi, Emperor Ming of Song's reign, the favorite Ruan Tianfu dominated the court; his halls were lavish and his equipage splendid; his carriage often tilted to one side, breaking the proper stance of holding the reins.

sentences.zh: 時人多慕效。

translations.literal: At the time many imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: Many at the time copied him.

sentences.zh: 此亦貌不恭之失也。

translations.literal: This too was a failure of appearance lacking respect.
translations.idiomatic: This was another lapse of deportment without respect.

sentences.zh: 時偏左之化行，方正之道廢矣。

translations.literal: Then the fashion of leaning left prevailed and the way of square correctness was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: A bias toward the left took hold, and upright propriety was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝常單騎遊遨，出入市里營寺，未嘗御輦。

translations.literal: Later the deposed emperor often rode out alone to roam, entering markets, wards, and monasteries, never using the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Later the deposed emperor often rode out alone, wandering through markets and monasteries, never taking the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 終以殞滅。

translations.literal: In the end he perished.
translations.idiomatic: He was destroyed in the end.

sentences.zh: 恒雨

translations.literal: Unending rain
translations.idiomatic: Unending Rain

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和元年秋，數大雨，多暴雷電，非常，至殺鳥雀。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Taihe of Emperor Ming of Wei, rain fell many times, with violent thunder and lightning beyond the norm, even killing birds.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Taihe, Emperor Ming of Wei's reign, rain fell repeatedly with thunder and lightning so violent that birds were killed.

sentences.zh: 案楊阜上蔬，此桓雨之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Yang Fu's memorial, this was the punishment of unending rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu's memorial identifies this as the penalty of unending rain.

sentences.zh: 時帝居喪不哀，出入弋獵無度，奢侈繁興，奪民農時，故木失其性而恒雨為災也。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor in mourning was not sorrowful, went out hunting without limit, luxury flourished, and farming seasons were stolen from the people; therefore wood lost its nature and unending rain became the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor observed mourning without grief, hunted without restraint, indulged luxury, and stole the people's farming seasons; wood lost its nature and unending rain followed.

sentences.zh: 太和四年八月，大雨霖三十餘日，伊、洛、河、漢皆溢，歲以凶饑。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe, heavy rain continued for more than thirty days; the Yi, Luo, Yellow, and Han rivers all overflowed, and the year ended in famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe rain poured for more than thirty days; the Yi, Luo, Yellow, and Han all burst their banks, and famine followed.

sentences.zh: 孫亮太平二年二月甲寅，大雨震電；

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the second month of the second year of Taiping of Sun Liang of Wu, heavy rain with thunder and lightning;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the second month of the second year of Taiping, Sun Liang of Wu's reign, torrential rain fell with thunder;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，雪，大寒。

translations.literal: on the yimao day, snow fell amid great cold.
translations.idiomatic: on the yimao day snow fell in bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 案劉歆說，此時當雨而不當大，大雨，恒雨之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xin's explanation, at this time rain was due but not in such abundance; great rain is the penalty of unending rain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin explains that rain was due then but not in such excess; excessive rain is the penalty called unending rain.

sentences.zh: 於始震電之明日而雪大寒，又恒寒之罰也。

translations.literal: That on the day after the first thunder and lightning snow and great cold came was again the penalty of unending cold.
translations.idiomatic: Snow and bitter cold the day after thunder was likewise the penalty of unending cold.

sentences.zh: 劉向以為既已震電，則雪不當復降，皆失時之異也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang held that once thunder and lightning had occurred, snow ought not to fall again—both were untimely anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang argued that after thunder snow should not return—both were violations of season.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，為君失時，賊臣將起。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning was as if to say: the ruler has lost the season and treacherous ministers will rise.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning said, as it were: the ruler has lost proper timing and rebel ministers will arise.

sentences.zh: 先震電而後雪者，陰見間隙，起而勝陽。

translations.literal: Thunder and lightning first and snow afterward means yin finds a gap, rises, and overcomes yang.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder first and snow after means yin seizes an opening, rises, and conquers yang.

sentences.zh: 逆殺之禍將及也。

translations.literal: The calamity of regicide drawing near was at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster of treason and murder was approaching.

sentences.zh: 亮不悟，尋見廢。

translations.literal: Liang did not understand and was soon deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang took no warning and was soon removed.

sentences.zh: 此與春秋魯隱同也。

translations.literal: This is the same matter as Duke Yin of Lu in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The case matches Duke Yin of Lu in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始六年六月，大雨霖，甲辰，河、洛、沁水同時並溢，流四千九百餘家，殺二百餘人，沒秋稼千三百六十餘頃。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, rain poured in torrents; on the jiachen day the Yellow, Luo, and Qin rivers overflowed together, flooding 4,900-odd households, killing more than 200 people, and drowning 1,360-odd qing of autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi, Emperor Wu of Jin's reign, rain poured without cease; on the jiachen day the Yellow, Luo, and Qin rivers burst together, drowning 4,900-odd households, killing more than 200 people, and ruining 1,360-odd qing of autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 晉武太康五年七月，任城、梁國暴雨，害豆麥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, Rencheng and Liang states had violent rain that harmed beans and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang, Rencheng and Liang were struck by violent rain that ruined beans and wheat.

sentences.zh: 太康五年九月，南安霖雨暴雪，折樹木，害秋稼；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Taikang, Nan'an had torrential rain and violent snow that broke trees and harmed autumn grain;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Taikang, Nan'an suffered torrential rain and blizzard that snapped trees and ruined the autumn crop;

sentences.zh: 魏郡、淮南、平原雨水，傷秋稼。

translations.literal: Wei commandery, Huainan, and Pingyuan had rain that injured autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Huainan, and Pingyuan were flooded and their autumn grain damaged.

sentences.zh: 是秋，魏郡、西平郡九縣霖雨暴水，霜傷秋稼。

translations.literal: That autumn, nine counties of Wei and Xiping commanderies had torrential rain and sudden flood; frost harmed autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn nine counties in Wei and Xiping were deluged and sudden floods followed; frost then ruined the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永寧元年十月，義陽、南陽、東海霖雨，淹害秋麥。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning of Emperor Hui of Jin, Yiyang, Nanyang, and Donghai had torrential rain that flooded and harmed autumn wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning, Yiyang, Nanyang, and Donghai were inundated and their autumn wheat destroyed.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康元年八月乙丑，荊州之長沙攸、醴陵、武陵之龍陽三縣，雨水浮漂屋室，殺人，傷損秋稼。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the eighth month of the first year of Xian'kang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, in the three counties of Changsha, You, and Longyang in Lingling of Jing Province, rain floated houses away, killed people, and damaged autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the eighth month of the first year of Xian'kang, rain in Changsha, You, and Longyang of Jing Province floated houses off their foundations, killed people, and ruined the autumn crop.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十一年六月，京邑連雨百餘日，大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, the capital had rain for more than a hundred days and great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, the capital rained for more than a hundred days and suffered great flooding.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明元年正月，京邑雨水。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the capital had rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Daming, the capital was deluged.

sentences.zh: 大明五年七月，京邑雨水。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Daming, the capital had rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Daming, the capital was deluged again.

sentences.zh: 大明八年八月，京邑雨水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year of Daming, the capital had rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eighth year of Daming, the capital was deluged again.

sentences.zh: 明帝太始二年六月，京邑雨水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, the capital had rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Taishi, Emperor Ming of Song's reign, the capital was deluged.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明三年四月乙亥，吳郡桐廬縣暴風雷電，揚砂折木，水平地二丈，流漂居民。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the fourth month of the third year of Shengming of Emperor Shun of Song, Tonglu county in Wu commandery had violent wind, thunder, and lightning; sand was whipped up and trees snapped; water stood two zhang above level ground and floated away the inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the fourth month of the third year of Shengming, Tonglu in Wu commandery was struck by wind, thunder, and lightning; sandstorms snapped trees and water rose two zhang above the plain, sweeping away the people.

sentences.zh: 服妖

translations.literal: Strange garments
translations.idiomatic: Strange Garments

sentences.zh: 魏武帝以天下凶荒，資財乏匱，始擬古皮弁，裁縑帛為白帢，以易舊服。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei, because the realm was stricken with famine and resources were exhausted, first took the ancient leather cap as model and cut silk cloth into white kerchiefs to replace the old dress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei, finding the realm famine-stricken and the treasury empty, modeled the ancient leather cap and cut silk into white kerchiefs to replace the old court dress.

sentences.zh: 傅玄曰：「白乃軍容，非國容也。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan said: "White is military dress, not the dress of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan said: "White belongs to military garb, not to the rites of state.

sentences.zh: 」干寶以為縞素，凶喪之象，帢，毀辱之言也。

translations.literal: " Gan Bao held that plain white silk is the image of funeral and mourning, and kerchief is speech of shame and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: " Gan Bao held that undyed silk symbolizes mourning and the kerchief speaks of shame.

sentences.zh: 蓋革代之後，攻殺之妖也。

translations.literal: Generally after a change of dynasty this is the portent of attack and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: After every dynastic overturn such dress marks the omen of war and slaughter.

sentences.zh: 初為白帢，橫縫其前以別後，名之曰「顏」，俗傳行之。

translations.literal: At first they made white kerchiefs with a cross-seam in front to distinguish back from front, calling it "face"; the vulgar transmitted and practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: At first the white kerchief bore a cross-seam in front to mark back from front, called "face," and the custom spread.

sentences.zh: 至晉永嘉之間，稍去其縫，名「無顏帢」。

translations.literal: By the Yongjia era of Jin the seam was gradually removed, and it was called the "faceless kerchief."
translations.idiomatic: By the Yongjia era the seam was abandoned and the cap was called "faceless."

sentences.zh: 而婦人束髮，其緩彌甚，紒之堅不能自立，髮被于額，目出而已。

translations.literal: Meanwhile women bound their hair ever more loosely; though twisted tight it could not stand, hair draped the forehead and only the eyes showed.
translations.idiomatic: Women bound their hair more and more loosely until, though twisted tight, it would not hold; hair covered the forehead and only the eyes remained visible.

sentences.zh: 無顏者，愧之言也；

translations.literal: "Faceless" is speech of shame;
translations.idiomatic: "Faceless" is the language of shame;

sentences.zh: 覆額者，慚之貌；

translations.literal: "covering the forehead" is the appearance of disgrace;
translations.idiomatic: covering the forehead is the look of humiliation;

sentences.zh: 其緩彌甚，言天下忘禮與義，放縱情性，及其終極，至乎大恥也。

translations.literal: ever looser binding means the realm forgot ritual and righteousness, indulged feeling and nature, and at the extreme reached great shame.
translations.idiomatic: ever looser binding means the empire forgot ritual and duty, indulged appetite and passion, and at last reached utter disgrace.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之後，二帝不反，天下愧焉。

translations.literal: After Yongjia the two emperors did not return; the realm was shamed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia the two emperors never came home and the world hung its head in shame.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝著繡帽，被縹紈半袖，嘗以見直臣楊阜。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei wore an embroidered cap and a light silk half-sleeve and once appeared thus before the blunt minister Yang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei wore an embroidered cap and a gauze half-sleeve and once received the blunt minister Yang Fu in that dress.

sentences.zh: 阜諫曰：「此於禮何法服邪？

translations.literal: Fu remonstrated: "By what ritual is this dress lawful?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu remonstrated: "What rite sanctions such clothing?"

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 近服妖也。

translations.literal: This is strange garments of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: This was a recent instance of strange garments.

sentences.zh: 縹，非禮之色，褻服不貳。

translations.literal: Light blue is not a color of ritual; intimate dress must not be doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Pale blue is no color of ritual, and private dress must not be duplicated for display.

sentences.zh: 今之人主，親御非法之章，所謂自作孽不可禳也。

translations.literal: When the ruler himself wears illegal insignia, it is what is called "self-inflicted calamity that cannot be averted."
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign himself dons unlawful regalia, it is the proverb: "He who brings calamity on himself cannot pray it away."

sentences.zh: 帝既不享永年，身沒而祿去王室，後嗣不終，遂亡天下。

translations.literal: The emperor did not enjoy a long reign; after his death salary left the royal house, the later line did not endure, and the realm was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He did not reign long; after his death stipends left the imperial house, his line failed, and the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初元年，發銅鑄為巨人二，號曰「翁仲」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu of Emperor Ming of Wei, copper was cast into two giant figures called "Wengzhong."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingchu, Emperor Ming of Wei cast copper into two giant figures called "Wengzhong."

sentences.zh: 置之司馬門外。

translations.literal: They were placed outside the Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They were set outside the Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 案古長人見，為國亡；

translations.literal: According to antiquity, when tall men appeared states perished;
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity records that when giants appeared states fell;

sentences.zh: 長狄見臨洮，為秦亡之禍。

translations.literal: when the Long Di appeared at Lintao it was the disaster of Qin's fall.
translations.idiomatic: when the Long Di appeared at Lintao it foretold Qin's ruin.

sentences.zh: 始皇不悟，反以為嘉祥，鑄銅人以象之。

translations.literal: The First Emperor did not understand and instead took it as auspicious, casting bronze men to imitate them.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor failed to understand and treated the omen as good fortune, casting bronze men in imitation.

sentences.zh: 魏法亡國之器，而於義竟無取焉。

translations.literal: Wei's law held that vessels of a perishing state were used; in righteousness there was nothing to be gained.
translations.idiomatic: Wei adopted the implements of doomed states—nothing righteous could come of it.

sentences.zh: 蓋服妖也。

translations.literal: Generally this was strange garments.
translations.idiomatic: In sum it was another case of strange garments.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書何晏，好服婦人之服。

translations.literal: He Yan of Wei, Director of the Secretariat, delighted in wearing women's dress.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, Director of the Secretariat under Wei, delighted in wearing women's clothing.

sentences.zh: 傅玄曰：「此服妖也。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan said: "This is strange garments.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan said: "This is strange garments.

sentences.zh: 」夫衣裳之制，所以定上下，殊內外也。

translations.literal: " The system of robes and skirts exists to fix upper and lower and to distinguish inner from outer.
translations.idiomatic: " Robes exist to fix rank above and below and to separate inner from outer.

sentences.zh: 大雅云：「玄袞赤舄，鉤膺鏤鍚。

translations.literal: The Greater Odes say: "Dark robes and red slippers, hooked breastplate and carved greaves.
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Odes sing: "Dark robes and red shoes, hooked breastplate and carved shin-guards.

sentences.zh: 」歌其文也。

translations.literal: " They sing its pattern.
translations.idiomatic: "—they praise its pattern.

sentences.zh: 小雅云：「有嚴有翼，共武之服。

translations.literal: The Lesser Odes say: "Stern and awe-inspiring, the martial king's dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Odes say: "Grave and majestic is the martial king's garb.

sentences.zh: 」詠其武也。

translations.literal: " They chant its martial bearing.
translations.idiomatic: "—they hymn its martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 若內外不殊，王制失敍，服妖既作，身隨之亡。

translations.literal: If inner and outer are not distinguished, royal order loses sequence; once strange garments arise, the person follows into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When inner and outer are not distinguished, royal order collapses; when strange garments appear, ruin follows the wearer.

sentences.zh: 末嬉冠男子之冠，桀亡天下；

translations.literal: Mo Xi wore a man's cap and Jie lost the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Mo Xi put on a man's cap and Jie lost the empire;

sentences.zh: 何晏服婦人之服，亦亡其家。

translations.literal: He Yan wore women's dress and likewise lost his house.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan wore women's clothing and his house was destroyed as well.

sentences.zh: 其咎均也。

translations.literal: Their faults were alike.
translations.idiomatic: Their offenses were the same.

sentences.zh: 吳婦人之修容者，急束其髮，而劘角過于耳。

translations.literal: Among Wu women who dressed their appearance, they bound the hair urgently and cut the corners past the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Wu women who dressed their hair bound it fiercely and trimmed the corners past the ears.

sentences.zh: 蓋其俗自操束大急，而廉隅失中之謂也。

translations.literal: Generally their custom of self-restraint was excessively tight, which is called losing the mean in integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Their custom of tight self-restraint overshot the mean of proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 故吳之風俗，相驅以急，言論彈射，以刻薄相尚。

translations.literal: Therefore Wu's customs drove one another to haste; in speech they shot barbs and honored one another with harshness.
translations.idiomatic: Wu folk drove one another to urgency, shot verbal barbs in debate, and prized harshness.

sentences.zh: 居三年之喪者，往往有致毀以死。

translations.literal: Those in the three-year mourning often brought themselves to ruin by emaciation and died.
translations.idiomatic: Mourners in the three-year rites often starved themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 諸葛患之，著正交論，雖不可以經訓整亂，蓋亦救時之作也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang was troubled by this and wrote the Discourse on Correct Friendship; though it could not set chaos in order by canonical teaching, it was nevertheless a work to rescue the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang, troubled by this, wrote the Discourse on Correct Friendship—not enough to restore order by the classics, yet a timely remedy.

sentences.zh: 孫休後，衣服之制，上長下短，又積領五六而裳居一二。

translations.literal: After Sun Xiu, the system of dress was long above and short below, with collars stacked five or six deep while the skirt occupied only one or two parts.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Xiu, garments grew long above and short below; collars piled five or six deep while the skirt shrank to a fraction.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「上饒奢，下儉逼，上有餘下不足之妖也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "Luxury above and stinginess below pressing upward—this is the portent of surplus above and insufficiency below.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "Extravagance above and meanness below—an omen of plenty on top and want underneath.

sentences.zh: 」至孫晧，果奢暴恣情於上，而百姓彫困於下，卒以亡國。

translations.literal: " By Sun Hao in the end he was extravagant and violent in feeling above while the common people were carved thin below, and in the end the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Sun Hao the ruler grew wanton and cruel while the people were ground down, and the state fell.

sentences.zh: 是其應也。

translations.literal: This was the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: This was the omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 晉興後，衣服上儉下豐，著衣者皆厭䙅蓋裙。

translations.literal: After Jin rose, upper garments were spare and lower garments abundant; those who dressed all wore overlapping skirts covering the lower robe.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin rose, the upper garment grew plain and the lower heavy; dressers wore layered skirts over their robes.

sentences.zh: 君衰弱，臣放縱，下掩上之象也。

translations.literal: The ruler weak and ministers unrestrained—an image of the lower covering the upper.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign weakened and ministers ran wild—the lower masking the upper.

sentences.zh: 陵遲至元康末，婦人出兩襠，加乎脛之上，此內出外也。

translations.literal: By the end of the Yuankang era women exposed both trouser legs above the shins—inner showing outward.
translations.idiomatic: By late Yuankang women bared both trouser legs above the calf—inner turned outward.

sentences.zh: 為車乘者，苟貴輕細，又數變易其形，皆以白篾為純，古喪車之遺象。

translations.literal: Those who rode carriages prized light and fine vehicles and changed their forms repeatedly, all using white bamboo as pure trim—the vestige of ancient mourning carts.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage owners prized light, delicate coaches and changed their style often, trimming everything in white bamboo like funeral carts.

sentences.zh: 乘者，君子之器，蓋君子立心無恒，事不崇實也。

translations.literal: The carriage is the gentleman's instrument; generally the gentleman's mind stands without constancy and affairs do not honor substance.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage is the gentleman's tool; when the gentleman's heart lacks constancy, affairs cease to rest on substance.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「及晉之禍，天子失柄，權制寵臣，下掩上之應也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "At the disaster of Jin the Son of Heaven lost the handle of power, authority rested with favored ministers, and the lower covered the upper—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "When Jin's calamity came the emperor lost the scepter, power sat with favorites, and the lower covered the upper.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，六宮才人，流徙戎、翟，內出外之應也。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia the palace women were driven off to the Rong and Di—again the response of inner going outward.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongjia's end palace women were swept to the northern tribes—inner cast outward again.

sentences.zh: 及天下亂擾，宰輔方伯，多負其任，又數改易，不崇實之應也。」

translations.literal: When the realm fell into turmoil, chief ministers and regional lords mostly failed their charge and changed office repeatedly—again the response of not honoring substance."
translations.idiomatic: When chaos spread, ministers and governors shirked duty and shifted posts endlessly—again the omen of hollow substance."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始後，中國相尚用胡牀、貊盤，及為羌煑、貊炙。

translations.literal: After Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, the Central States came to favor barbarian couches, Mo platters, and Qiang stews and Mo roasts.
translations.idiomatic: After Taishi, the heartland took to barbarian couches, Mo platters, and Qiang boiled meat and Mo roasts.

sentences.zh: 貴人富室，必置其器，吉享嘉會，皆此為先。

translations.literal: The wealthy and great houses had to set out these vessels; at auspicious feasts and fine gatherings they came first.
translations.idiomatic: Rich households kept such wares; at every feast they took pride of place.

sentences.zh: 太康中，天下又以氈為絈頭及絡帶、衿口。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era the realm also used felt for kerchief heads, web belts, and collar openings.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang felt was used for head-wraps, belts, and collar bands.

sentences.zh: 百姓相戲曰，中國必為胡所破也。

translations.literal: The common people jested that the Central States would surely be broken by the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: People joked that the heartland would be overrun by the Hu.

sentences.zh: 氈產於胡，而天下以為絈頭、帶身、衿口，胡既三制之矣，能无敗乎。

translations.literal: Felt comes from the Hu, yet the realm took it for kerchief head, belt body, and collar opening—the Hu had already made three parts of the dress; how could there be no defeat?
translations.idiomatic: Felt is a Hu product, yet the empire wore it on head, belt, and collar—three Hu marks on the body; how could it not fall?

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「元康中，氐、羌反，至于永嘉，劉淵、石勒遂有中都。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "In Yuankang the Di and Qiang rebelled; by Yongjia Liu Yuan and Shi Le held the central capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao wrote: "In Yuankang the Di and Qiang rose; by Yongjia Liu Yuan and Shi Le seized the central capital.

sentences.zh: 自後四夷迭據華土，是其應也。」

translations.literal: Afterward the four barbarians in turn occupied the Hua lands—this was the fulfillment."
translations.idiomatic: Then the four tribes held the heartland in turn—the omen fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康後，天下為家者，移婦人於東方，空萊北庭，以為園囿。

translations.literal: After Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, households that built homes moved the women's quarters to the east and emptied the northern court of Lai for gardens.
translations.idiomatic: After Taikang, builders moved women's quarters eastward and turned the northern court into gardens.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「夫王朝南向，正陽也；

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "The royal court faces south—the position of true yang;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "The court faces south, the seat of true yang;

sentences.zh: 后北宮，位太陰也；

translations.literal: the empress occupies the northern palace, the seat of great yin;
translations.idiomatic: the empress holds the northern palace, the seat of great yin;

sentences.zh: 世子居東宮，位少陽也。

translations.literal: the heir apparent dwells in the eastern palace, the seat of lesser yang.
translations.idiomatic: the heir dwells in the eastern palace, the seat of lesser yang.

sentences.zh: 今居內於東，是與外俱南面也。

translations.literal: Now to lodge the inner quarters in the east is to face outward together with the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Now lodging the inner quarters in the east makes them face south like the outer court.

sentences.zh: 亢陽无陰，婦人失位而干少陽之象也。

translations.literal: Excessive yang without yin—women lose their place and interfere with lesser yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang overwhelms yin—women leave their station and usurp lesser yang.

sentences.zh: 賈后讒戮愍懷，俄而禍敗亦及。」

translations.literal: Empress Jia slandered and killed Emperor Huai's heir; soon disaster and ruin overtook her as well."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia destroyed the heir of Emperor Huai; soon ruin overtook her too."

sentences.zh: 昔初作履者，婦人圓頭，男子方頭。

translations.literal: In antiquity when shoes were first made, women had round toes and men square toes.
translations.idiomatic: When shoes were first fashioned, women wore round toes and men square.

sentences.zh: 圓者，順從之義，所以別男女也。

translations.literal: Round means the meaning of compliance, whereby men and women were distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Round signified yielding obedience and marked the sexes apart.

sentences.zh: 晉太康初，婦人皆履方頭，此去其圓從，與男無別也。

translations.literal: In the early Taikang era of Jin all women wore square toes—casting off round compliance and becoming no different from men.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang every woman wore square toes—abandoning round obedience and matching men.

sentences.zh: 太康之中，天下為晉世寧之舞，手接杯槃反覆之，歌曰：「晉世寧，舞杯槃。

translations.literal: In the midst of Taikang the realm had the dance "Jin World at Peace," hands catching cups and platters and turning them over, singing: "Jin world at peace, dance with cups and platters.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Taikang produced the "Jin World at Peace" dance, tossing cups and platters hand to hand, with the song: "Jin world at peace—dance the cups and platters.

sentences.zh: 」夫樂生人心，所以觀事。

translations.literal: " Music arises in the human heart and therefore serves to observe affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Music springs from the heart and reveals the age.

sentences.zh: 故記曰：「總干山立，武王之事也；

translations.literal: Therefore the Record says: "The chief staffs stand like mountains—this was King Wu's affair;
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "Banners stand like mountains—that was King Wu's deed;

sentences.zh: 發揚蹈厲，太公之志也；

translations.literal: to display and tread vigorously was Grand Duke Jiang's ambition;
translations.idiomatic: to brandish and stamp hard was the Grand Duke Jiang's will;

sentences.zh: 武亂皆坐，周、召之治也。

translations.literal: martial disorder all seated—this was the governance of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: martial frenzy all seated—that was Zhou and Shao's order.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「其治民勞者，舞行綴遠；

translations.literal: " It also says: "Where government wearies the people, the dance rows are far apart;
translations.idiomatic: " Where rule wearies the people, dance rows stand far apart;

sentences.zh: 其治民逸者，舞行綴近。

translations.literal: where government rests the people, the dance rows are close.
translations.idiomatic: where rule rests the people, dance rows stand close.

sentences.zh: 今接杯槃於手上而反覆之，至危也。

translations.literal: Now catching cups and platters in the hand and turning them over reaches the point of peril.
translations.idiomatic: Now to catch cups and platters in the hand and flip them is peril itself.

sentences.zh: 杯槃者，酒食之器也，而名曰晉世寧者，言晉世之士，偷苟於酒食之間，而其知不及遠，晉世之寧，猶杯槃之在手也。」

translations.literal: Cups and platters are vessels of food and drink, yet they are named "Jin World at Peace"—meaning that scholars of Jin steal ease among food and drink, their understanding not reaching far; the peace of the Jin age is still like cups and platters in the hand."
translations.idiomatic: Cups and platters are for food and drink, yet the name says "Jin World at Peace"—Jin gentlemen snatch comfort at table, their vision no farther than the rim; Jin's peace is only what cups hold in the palm."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，婦人之飾有五兵佩，又以金、銀、瑇瑁之屬為斧、鉞、戈、戟，以當笄□。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, women's adornments included the Five Weapons pendant, and gold, silver, and tortoise-shell were fashioned into axes, yue, ge, and ji to serve as hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang, women wore Five Weapons pendants; gold, silver, and tortoise shell were shaped into axes, halberds, spears, and ji for hairpins.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「男女之別，國之大節，故服物異等，贄幣不同。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "The distinction of man and woman is the great statute of the state; therefore dress objects differ in grade and tribute gifts differ.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "Male and female are the state's great boundary; dress and gifts must differ.

sentences.zh: 今婦人而以兵器為飾，又妖之大也。

translations.literal: Now women take weapons for ornament—again a great portent.
translations.idiomatic: When women arm themselves for ornament, the omen is grave.

sentences.zh: 遂有賈后之事，終以兵亡天下。」

translations.literal: Soon came the affair of Empress Jia, and in the end arms lost the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Soon came Empress Jia's plot, and arms lost the empire."

sentences.zh: 元康中，婦人結髮者，既成，以繒急束其環，名曰擷子紒。

translations.literal: In Yuankang, women who bound their hair, once done, bound the ring urgently with silk, called "pinching the knot."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang women, once the hair was bound, cinched the ring tight with silk—the "pinching knot."

sentences.zh: 始自中宮，天下化之。

translations.literal: It began in the inner palace and the realm took it as model.
translations.idiomatic: It began in the inner palace and the world copied it.

sentences.zh: 其後賈后果害太子。

translations.literal: Afterward Empress Jia indeed harmed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Jia destroyed the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 元康中，天下始相倣為㮧杖，以柱掖其後，稍施其錞，住則植之。

translations.literal: In Yuankang the realm first imitated one another in making zhu staffs, using them to prop the armpit from behind, gradually adding the metal cap; when stopping they planted it in the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang people copied zhu staffs to brace the armpit, added metal caps, and planted them when they halted.

sentences.zh: 夫木，東方之行，金之臣也。

translations.literal: Wood is the agent of the east, minister to metal.
translations.idiomatic: Wood is the eastern agent, servant to metal.

sentences.zh: 扶者，杖體之器，㮧其頭者，尤便用也。

translations.literal: The support is the instrument of the staff's body; zhu at the head is especially convenient in use.
translations.idiomatic: The staff supports the body; a zhu head makes it handier.

sentences.zh: 必傍柱掖者，傍救之象也。

translations.literal: Surely to lean on a side pillar is the image of rescue from the side.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on a side prop images rescue from the flank.

sentences.zh: 王室多故，而元帝以蕃臣樹德東方，維持天下，柱掖之應也。

translations.literal: The royal house had many troubles, and Emperor Yuan as a feudal prince planted virtue in the east and upheld the realm—the response of pillar support.
translations.idiomatic: The house had many woes; Emperor Yuan as a prince rooted virtue in the east and held the realm up—the prop omen.

sentences.zh: 至社稷無主，海內歸之，遂承天命，建都江外，獨立之應也。

translations.literal: When the altars had no lord and the realm turned to him, he then received the Mandate, established the capital beyond the river, and stood alone—the response of standing apart.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne stood empty the realm turned to him; he took the Mandate, built the capital south of the Yangtze, and stood alone—the solitary omen.

sentences.zh: 元康末至太安間，江、淮之域，有敗編自聚于道，多者或至四五十量。

translations.literal: From the end of Yuankang to the Tai'an period, in the Jiang-Huai region tattered hemp gathered of itself on the roads, sometimes forty or fifty bundles.
translations.idiomatic: From late Yuankang through Tai'an, tattered hemp piled itself on Jiang-Huai roads, sometimes forty or fifty bundles.

sentences.zh: 干寶嘗使人散而去之，或投林草，或投坑谷。

translations.literal: Gan Bao once sent men to scatter it, casting it into woods and grass or into pits and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao once had men scatter the piles into woods or ravines.

sentences.zh: 明日視之，悉復如故。

translations.literal: The next day when they looked, all was as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day everything had returned as before.

sentences.zh: 民或云見狸銜而聚之，亦未察也。

translations.literal: The people said they saw raccoon dogs carrying and gathering it, but this too was not examined.
translations.idiomatic: Some said raccoon dogs gathered it; no one verified the tale.

sentences.zh: 寶說曰：「夫編者，人之賤服，最處于下，而當勞辱，下民之象也。

translations.literal: Bao explained: "Hemp cloth is the mean dress of men, lowest in place and subject to labor and insult—the image of the lower people.
translations.idiomatic: Bao explained: "Hemp is the poor man's cloth, lowest and worn with toil—the image of commoners.

sentences.zh: 敗者，疲斃之象也。

translations.literal: "Tattered" is the image of exhaustion and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: "Tattered" images exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 道者，地理四方，所以交通王命所由往來也。

translations.literal: "The Way" is the geography of the four directions whereby royal commands travel to and fro.
translations.idiomatic: "The road" is the land of four directions where royal commands pass.

sentences.zh: 故今敗編聚於道者，象下民罷病，將相聚為亂，絕四方而壅王命之象也。

translations.literal: Therefore tattered hemp now gathering on the Way means the image of the lower people weary and sick, about to gather in rebellion, cutting off the four directions and blocking royal commands.
translations.idiomatic: Tattered hemp on the roads means commoners broken and about to rebel, severing the realm from royal command.

sentences.zh: 在位者莫察。

translations.literal: Those in office did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power never looked into it.

sentences.zh: 太安中，發壬午兵，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an period they raised the renwu army; the common people sighed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai'an the renwu army was raised and the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 江夏男子張昌遂首亂荊楚，從之者如流。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang, a man of Jiangxia, then first raised rebellion in Jing-Chu, and those who followed flowed like a stream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang of Jiangxia first rebelled in Jing-Chu; followers poured in.

sentences.zh: 於是兵革歲起，天下因之，遂大破壞。

translations.literal: Then arms and armor rose year by year; because of this the realm was greatly broken.
translations.idiomatic: War followed year after year until the realm lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 此近服妖也。」

translations.literal: This is strange garments of recent times."
translations.idiomatic: This too was recent strange garments."

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷永嘉以來，士大夫竟服生箋單衣。

translations.literal: From Yongjia of Emperor Xiaohuai of Jin onward, scholar-officials all wore raw hemp single garments.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongjia onward gentlemen wore unbleached hemp single robes.

sentences.zh: 遠識者怪之，竊指擿曰：「此則古者繐衰之布，諸侯大夫所以服天子也。

translations.literal: Men of far sight found it strange and privately pointed and said: "This is the cloth of the fringed mourning garment with which feudal lords and great ministers served the Son of Heaven in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The far-sighted whispered: "This is the hemp of ancient fringed mourning in which lords served the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今無故畢服之，殆有應乎？

translations.literal: Now to wear it entirely without cause—will there not be a response?"
translations.idiomatic: To wear it now without cause—will not the omen answer?"

sentences.zh: 」其後愍、懷晏駕，不獲厥所。

translations.literal: Afterward Emperors Min and Huai died on the road and did not obtain their proper resting place.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperors Min and Huai died on the road without proper burial.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興以來，兵士以絳囊縛紒。

translations.literal: From Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin onward, soldiers bound their topknots with crimson pouches.
translations.idiomatic: From Taixing onward soldiers bound their topknots in crimson pouches.

sentences.zh: 紒在首，莫上焉。

translations.literal: The topknot is on the head—nothing is above it.
translations.idiomatic: The topknot sits on the head—nothing stands above.

sentences.zh: 周易乾為首，坤為囊。

translations.literal: In the Book of Changes, Qian is the head and Kun is the pouch.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes Qian the head and Kun the pouch.

sentences.zh: 坤，臣道也。

translations.literal: Kun is the way of the minister.
