translations.idiomatic: Kun is the minister's way.

sentences.zh: 晉金行，赤火色，金之賊也。

translations.literal: Jin's element is metal; red is the color of fire, enemy to metal.
translations.idiomatic: Jin belongs to metal; red is fire, metal's destroyer.

sentences.zh: 以朱囊縛紒，臣道上侵之象也。

translations.literal: To bind the topknot with a crimson pouch is the image of the minister's way pressing upward.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson pouches on the topknot image ministers pressing upward.

sentences.zh: 到永昌元年，大將軍王敦舉兵內攻，六軍散潰。

translations.literal: By the first year of Yongchang, the Grand General Wang Dun raised troops to attack within; the six armies scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang Grand General Wang Dun marched on the capital and the six armies broke.

sentences.zh: 舊為羽扇，柄刻木，象其骨形，羽用十，取全數也。

translations.literal: Formerly feather fans had handles carved in wood imitating bone form; feathers used ten, taking the full number.
translations.idiomatic: Feather fans once had wooden handles carved like bone and used ten feathers for the full count.

sentences.zh: 晉中興初，王敦南征，始改為長柄下出，可捉，而減其羽用八。

translations.literal: In the early Zhongxing era of Jin, when Wang Dun marched south he first changed them to long handles extending below so they could be grasped, and reduced the feathers to eight.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhongxing, when Wang Dun marched south, he lengthened the handle below for a grip and cut the feathers to eight.

sentences.zh: 識者尤之曰：「夫羽扇，翼之名也。

translations.literal: Observers especially faulted it: "The feather fan is the name of wings.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said: "The feather fan is named for wings.

sentences.zh: 創為長柄者，執其柄制羽翼也。

translations.literal: To make a long handle is to grasp the handle and control the wings.
translations.idiomatic: A long handle means seizing the shaft to command the wings.

sentences.zh: 以十改八者，將以未備奪已備也。

translations.literal: To change from ten to eight is to let the not-yet-ready seize the already-ready."
translations.idiomatic: Cutting ten to eight lets the unprepared seize the prepared."

sentences.zh: 」是時為衣者，又上短，帶至于掖；

translations.literal: " At that time those who made clothes also made the upper short, belts reaching only to the armpit;
translations.idiomatic: Then dressers shortened the upper garment until belts reached only the armpit;

sentences.zh: 著帽者，以帶縛項。

translations.literal: those who wore caps bound the band around the neck.
translations.idiomatic: cap-wearers bound the band around the neck.

sentences.zh: 下逼上，上無地也。

translations.literal: The lower pressing the upper—above there is no ground.
translations.idiomatic: Below pressing above—nothing remains overhead.

sentences.zh: 下袴者，直幅為口無殺，下大失裁也。

translations.literal: Lower trousers were straight-cut openings without taper; the lower part greatly lost proper cut.
translations.idiomatic: Trousers were cut straight without shaping—the lower garment lost all fit.

sentences.zh: 尋有兵亂，三年而再攻京師。

translations.literal: Soon there was military disorder; within three years the capital was attacked twice.
translations.idiomatic: War followed; within three years the capital was attacked twice.

sentences.zh: 晉海西初嗣位，迎官忘設豹尾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hai of Jin first succeeded, in welcoming the officials they forgot to set out the leopard tail.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hai of Jin first took the throne, the welcoming party forgot the leopard-tail insignia.

sentences.zh: 識者以為不終之象，近服妖也。

translations.literal: Observers held it an image of not reaching the end—strange garments of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Observers called it an omen of no completion—recent strange garments.

sentences.zh: 晉司馬道子於府北園內為酒鑪列肆，使姬人酤鬻酒肴，如裨販者，數遊其中，身自買易，因醉寓寢，動連日夜。

translations.literal: Sima Daozi of Jin set up wine shops in rows in the northern garden of his mansion, had concubines sell wine and food like peddlers, and often wandered among them, buying and selling himself; he would get drunk and lodge there, sometimes for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi opened wine stalls in his north garden, had concubines hawk food like hucksters, wandered among them buying and selling, and slept there drunk for days.

sentences.zh: 漢靈帝嘗若此。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling of Han once did the same.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling of Han had done likewise.

sentences.zh: 干寶以為：「君將失位，降在皁隸之象也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao held that "the ruler is about to lose position and descend to the rank of menials."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao read it as "the ruler about to fall to the status of a servant."

sentences.zh: 」道子卒見廢徙，以庶人終。

translations.literal: " Daozi in the end was deposed and banished and ended as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: " Daozi was deposed, exiled, and died a commoner.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡立，殿上施絳綾帳，鏤黃金為顏，四角金龍，銜五色羽葆流蘇。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, crimson silk curtains were hung in the hall, gold carved for faces, golden dragons at the four corners holding five-colored feather streamers.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped, crimson silk curtains hung in the hall, gold faces carved on them, golden dragons at the corners bearing five-colored feather streamers.

sentences.zh: 羣下竊相謂曰：「頗類輀車。

translations.literal: The crowd whispered to one another: "It rather resembles a funeral carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers whispered: "It looks much like a funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 」此服妖也。

translations.literal: " This is strange garments.
translations.idiomatic: " This too was strange garments.

sentences.zh: 晉末皆冠小冠，而衣裳博大，風流相倣，輿臺成俗。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin all wore small caps while robes and skirts were broad and flowing; elegance was imitated and the custom spread even to runners and menials.
translations.idiomatic: Late Jin gentlemen wore small caps with billowing robes; the fashion spread even to servants.

sentences.zh: 識者曰：「此禪代之象也。

translations.literal: Observers said: "This is the image of the transfer of the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said: "This foretells the transfer of the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 」永初以後，冠還大云。

translations.literal: " After Yongchu caps again grew large.
translations.idiomatic: " After Yongchu caps grew large again.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉六年，民間婦人結髮者，三分髮，抽其鬟直向上，謂之「飛天紒」。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, among folk women who bound their hair, they divided the hair in three parts, drew the bun straight upward, and called it "flying-heaven knot."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanjia, women divided their hair in three parts and drew the bun straight up, calling it the "flying-heaven knot."

sentences.zh: 始自東府，流被民庶。

translations.literal: It began in the Eastern Mansion and spread to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: It began in the Eastern Mansion and spread to the populace.

sentences.zh: 時司徒彭城王義康居東府，其後卒以陵上徙廢。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Pengcheng, Liu Yikang, as Director of the Secretariat dwelt in the Eastern Mansion; afterward he was banished for overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: Then Director Liu Yikang of Pengcheng lived in the Eastern Mansion; he was later removed for arrogance.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝世，豫州刺史劉德願善御車，世祖嘗使之御畫輪，幸太宰江夏王義恭第。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Liu Deyuan, Inspector of Yu Province, was skilled at driving carriages; the emperor once had him drive the painted wheel carriage to visit the Grand Tutor, the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowu's era Liu Deyuan of Yu Province was a skilled driver; the emperor had him drive the painted carriage to visit Grand Tutor Liu Yigong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 德願挾牛杖催世祖云：「日暮宜歸！

translations.literal: Deyuan, clutching an ox-goad, urged the emperor: "The sun is setting—you should return!
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan, ox-goad in hand, urged him: "The sun is low—it is time to go home!

sentences.zh: 」又求益僦車。

translations.literal: " He also asked for more hire for the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked for a higher carriage fee.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚歡。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 此事與漢靈帝西園蓄私錢同也。

translations.literal: This matter is the same as Emperor Ling of Han storing private money in the Western Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The episode matches Emperor Ling of Han hoarding private money in the Western Garden.

sentences.zh: 孝武世，幸臣戴法興權亞人主，造圓頭履，世人莫不效之。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the favorite Dai Faxing's power was second only to the ruler; he made round-toed shoes and none in the realm failed to copy him.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowu's era the favorite Dai Faxing rivaled the throne; he devised round-toed shoes and the world copied them.

sentences.zh: 其時圓進之俗大行，方格之風盡矣。

translations.literal: At that time the fashion of round advance prevailed and the style of square correctness was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Round fashion triumphed and square propriety vanished.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，司徒建安王休仁統軍赭圻，制烏紗帽，反抽帽裙，民間謂之「司徒狀」，京邑翕然相尚。

translations.literal: In the early Ming era, the Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, commanding at Zheqi, devised black gauze caps with the hat skirt turned back—folk called it "Director's style," and the capital rushed to imitate it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ming, Liu Xiuren of Jian'an at Zheqi devised black gauze caps with the skirt reversed—"Director's style," which the capital imitated.

sentences.zh: 休仁後果以疑逼致禍。

translations.literal: Xiuren afterward indeed met disaster through suspicion and coercion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren later fell to suspicion and was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 龜孽

translations.literal: Tortoise portents
translations.idiomatic: Tortoise Portents

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永熙初，衛瓘家人炊飯，墮地，盡化為螺，出足起行。

translations.literal: In the early Yongxi era of Emperor Hui of Jin, in the household of Wei Guan when cooking rice it fell to the ground and all turned into snails that put out feet, rose, and walked.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi, rice in Wei Guan's kitchen fell to the floor and turned into snails that sprouted feet and crawled away.

sentences.zh: 螺，龜類，近龜孽也。

translations.literal: Snails are of the tortoise kind and are near to tortoise portents.
translations.idiomatic: Snails belong to the tortoise family and count as near tortoise omens.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「螺被甲，兵象也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "Snails wear armor—the image of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "Snails wear armor—the sign of war.

sentences.zh: 於周易為離，離為戈兵。

translations.literal: In the Book of Changes this is Li, and Li is spear and weapon.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Changes this is Li, the trigram of weapons.

sentences.zh: 」明年，瓘誅。

translations.literal: " The next year Guan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year Guan was executed.

sentences.zh: 雞禍

translations.literal: Chicken calamities
translations.idiomatic: Chicken Calamities

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初二年，廷尉府中有雌雞變為雄，不鳴不將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingchu of Emperor Ming of Wei, in the Ministry of Justice there was a hen that changed into a cock, neither crowing nor leading.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingchu a hen in the Ministry of Justice turned into a cock that neither crowed nor led the flock.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「是歲，晉宣帝平遼東，百姓始有與能之議，此其象也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "That year the Jin Emperor Xuan pacified Liaodong and the common people first had talk of ability to replace—this was its sign.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "That year Emperor Xuan of Jin pacified Liaodong and people first spoke of replacing the house of Cao—its sign.

sentences.zh: 」然晉三后並以人臣終，不鳴不將，又天意也。

translations.literal: " Yet the three empresses of Jin all ended as subjects and did not crow or lead—again Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Jin's three empresses all died as subjects without crowing or leading—Heaven's intent as well.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康六年，陳國有雞生雄雞無翅，既大，墜坑而死。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, in Chen state a cock was born from a hen without wings; when grown it fell into a pit and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuankang a hen in Chen bore a wingless cock that later fell into a pit and died.

sentences.zh: 王隱曰：「雄，胤嗣象，坑地事為母象，賈后誣殺愍懷，殆其應也。」

translations.literal: Wang Yin said: "The cock is the image of male heirs; the pit is the image of the mother's affair—Empress Jia slandered and killed Emperor Huai's heir; this is likely the fulfillment."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin said: "The cock images the heir; the pit images the mother—Empress Jia destroyed Emperor Huai's son; likely the fulfillment."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安中，周玘家有雌雞逃承霤中，六七日而下，奮翼鳴將，獨毛羽不變。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an period of Emperor Hui of Jin, in Zhou Ji's household a hen fled into the eaves gutter; after six or seven days it came down, flapped its wings and crowed to lead, yet its feathers alone did not change.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai'an a hen in Zhou Ji's house fled into the eaves, then descended days later crowing like a cock while its feathers stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其後有陳敏之事。

translations.literal: Afterward came the affair of Chen Min.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward came Chen Min's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 敏雖控制江表，終無綱紀文章，殆其象也。

translations.literal: Min though he controlled the Jiang region in the end had no statutes or literary order—likely its sign.
translations.idiomatic: Min held the lower Yangtze yet never established proper rule—the omen's meaning.

sentences.zh: 卒為玘所滅。

translations.literal: In the end he was destroyed by Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji destroyed him in the end.

sentences.zh: 雞禍見玘家，又天意也。

translations.literal: The chicken calamity appeared in Ji's house—again Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The chicken omen appeared in Ji's house—again Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興中，王敦鎮武昌，有雌雞化為雄。

translations.literal: In the Taixing period of Emperor Yuan of Jin, when Wang Dun garrisoned Wuchang, a hen changed into a cock.
translations.idiomatic: During Taixing, while Wang Dun held Wuchang, a hen turned into a cock.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰：「雌化為雄，臣陵其上。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning was as if to say: "The female turns male—the subject towers over his superior.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven warned: "Female becomes male—the minister overtops his lord.

sentences.zh: 」其後王敦再攻京師。

translations.literal: " Afterward Wang Dun again attacked the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Dun attacked the capital again.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元十三年四月，廣陵高平閻嵩家雄雞，生無右翅；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, at Yan Song's house in Gaoping, Guangling, a cock was born without its right wing;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan, a cock at Yan Song's house in Gaoping, Guangling, was born without its right wing;

sentences.zh: 彭城到象之家雞，無右足。

translations.literal: at Dao Xiang's house in Pengcheng a chicken had no right foot.
translations.idiomatic: at Dao Xiang's house in Pengcheng a chicken lacked its right foot.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「君用婦人言，則雞生妖。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes says: "When the ruler heeds women's words, chickens produce portents."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes says: "When a ruler listens to women, chickens grow strange."

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安元年八月，琅邪王道子家青雌雞化為赤雄，不鳴不將。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Long'an of Emperor An of Jin, at the house of the Prince of Langya, Sima Daozi, a blue hen changed into a red cock, neither crowing nor leading.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Long'an, a blue hen at Sima Daozi's house turned into a red cock that neither crowed nor led.

sentences.zh: 後有桓玄之事，具如其象。

translations.literal: Afterward came the affair of Huan Xuan, fully matching its sign.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's usurpation followed, matching the sign completely.

sentences.zh: 隆安四年，荊州有雞生角，角尋墮落。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, in Jing Province a chicken grew horns, which soon fell off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Long'an a chicken in Jing Province grew horns that soon dropped off.

sentences.zh: 是時桓玄始擅西夏，狂慢不肅，故有雞禍。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Xuan first dominated the western regions, arrogant and without reverence; therefore there was the chicken calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Then Huan Xuan dominated the west, arrogant and unrestrained—hence the chicken omen.

sentences.zh: 角，兵象；

translations.literal: Horns are the image of arms;
translations.idiomatic: Horns image weapons;

sentences.zh: 尋墮落者，暫起不終之妖也。

translations.literal: soon falling off is the portent of rising briefly and not enduring.
translations.idiomatic: their quick fall images a rise that cannot last.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興二年，衡陽有雌雞化為雄，八十日而冠萎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxing of Emperor An of Jin, in Hengyang a hen changed into a cock; after eighty days its comb withered.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanxing, in Hengyang a hen became a cock; after eighty days its comb wilted.

sentences.zh: 衡陽，桓玄楚國封略也。

translations.literal: Hengyang was within the territorial extent of Huan Xuan's state of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Hengyang lay within Huan Xuan's Chu domain.

sentences.zh: 後篡位八十日而敗，徐廣以為玄之象也。

translations.literal: Afterward he usurped the throne for eighty days and was defeated; Xu Guang held this to be Xuan's sign.
translations.idiomatic: He usurped for eighty days and fell; Xu Guang took it as Xuan's omen.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十二年，華林園雌雞漸化為雄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, in the Hualin Garden a hen gradually changed into a cock.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia a hen in the Hualin Garden slowly turned into a cock.

sentences.zh: 後孝武即位，皇太后令行于外，亦猶漢宣帝時，雌雞為雄，至哀帝時，元后與政也。

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne and the empress dowager issued commands abroad—again like the time of Emperor Xuan of Han, when the hen became cock until the era of Emperor Ai, when the Grand Empress Dowager Wang took part in government.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowu reigned and the empress dowager governed abroad—as under Emperor Xuan of Han, when hens turned cock until Emperor Ai, when the Grand Empress Dowager ruled.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始中，吳興東遷沈法符家雞有四距。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Emperor Ming of Song, at Shen Fafu's house in Dongqian, Wuxing, a chicken had four spurs.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi, a chicken at Shen Fafu's house in Dongqian, Wuxing, bore four spurs.

sentences.zh: 青眚青祥

translations.literal: Blue calamities and blue omens
translations.idiomatic: Blue Calamities and Blue Omens

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧元年八月丁酉，大風折太社樹，有青氣出焉。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the eighth month of the first year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, a great wind broke the tree of the Grand Altar and blue vapor issued from it.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the eighth month of the first year of Xianning, a great wind snapped the Grand Altar tree and blue vapor rose from it.

sentences.zh: 此青祥也。

translations.literal: This was a blue omen.
translations.idiomatic: This was a blue portent.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「東莞當有帝者。

translations.literal: According to divination: "Dongguan will have one who becomes emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Divination read: "Dongguan will produce an emperor.

sentences.zh: 」明年，元帝生。

translations.literal: " The next year Emperor Yuan was born.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year Emperor Yuan was born.

sentences.zh: 是時帝大父武王封東莞，由是徙封琅邪。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's great-grandfather the Prince of Wu was enfeoffed in Dongguan; because of this the fief was moved to Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Then the emperor's great-grandfather, Prince of Wu, held Dongguan; the fief was later moved to Langya.

sentences.zh: 孫盛以為中興之表。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng held this to be the sign of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng took it as the sign of Jin's restoration.

sentences.zh: 晉室之亂，武帝子孫無孑遺，社樹折之應，又恒風之罰也。

translations.literal: In the disorder of the Jin house, none of Emperor Wu's sons and grandsons survived; the response of the altar tree breaking was also the punishment of unending wind.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell into chaos, Emperor Wu's line perished to the last man—the broken altar tree and unending wind were its omens.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，洛陽南山有䖟作聲曰：「韓屍屍。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, on the southern mountain of Luoyang flies made a sound saying "Han corpse corpse."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang, flies on Luoyang's southern mountain buzzed "Han corpse corpse."

sentences.zh: 」識者曰：「韓氏將死也。

translations.literal: Observers said: "The Han clan is about to die.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said: "The Han clan will perish.

sentences.zh: 言屍屍者，盡死意也。

translations.literal: Saying corpse corpse means the meaning of all dead.
translations.idiomatic: Corpse corpse means all are dead."

sentences.zh: 」其後韓謐誅而韓族殲焉。

translations.literal: " Afterward Han Mi was executed and the Han clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Han Mi was executed and the Han clan wiped out.

sentences.zh: 此青祥也。

translations.literal: This was a blue omen.
translations.idiomatic: This was a blue portent.

sentences.zh: 金沴木

translations.literal: Metal harms wood
translations.idiomatic: Metal Harms Wood

sentences.zh: 魏文帝初七年正月，幸許昌。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei, he visited Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year of his reign, Emperor Wen of Wei visited Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 許昌城南門無故自崩，帝心惡之，遂不入，還洛陽。

translations.literal: The southern gate of Xuchang city for no reason collapsed of itself; the emperor's heart was troubled, and he did not enter but returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchang's southern gate collapsed without cause; the emperor took it ill, did not enter, and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 此金沴木，木動也。

translations.literal: This was metal harming wood—wood moved.
translations.idiomatic: This was metal harming wood—wood stirred.

sentences.zh: 五月，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the palace carriage halted at dusk—the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the palace carriage stopped at dusk—the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「上下咸悖，厥妖城門壞。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes says: "When above and below are all rebellious, the portent is city gates breaking."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes says: "When high and low alike rebel, city gates break."

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興二年六月，吳郡米廩無故自壞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, the grain storehouse of Wu commandery for no reason collapsed of itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Taixing, Wu commandery's grain storehouse collapsed on its own.

sentences.zh: 是歲大饑，死者數千。

translations.literal: That year there was great famine and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine killed thousands.

sentences.zh: 晉明帝太寧元年，周筵自歸王敦，既立宅宇，而所起五間六架，一時躍出墮地，餘桁猶亘柱頭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taining of Emperor Ming of Jin, Zhou Yan returned to Wang Dun; having built his residence, the five bays and six frames he raised all at once leaped out and fell to the ground, the remaining rafters still spanning the pillar heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taining, Zhou Yan joined Wang Dun; the five-bay, six-frame hall he built leaped from its site, rafters still caught on the pillars.

sentences.zh: 此金沴木也。

translations.literal: This was metal harming wood.
translations.idiomatic: This was metal harming wood.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，錢鳳謀亂，遂族滅筵，而湖熟尋亦為墟矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year Qian Feng plotted rebellion; Yan's clan was exterminated, and Hushu soon became ruins as well.
translations.idiomatic: The next fifth month Qian Feng rebelled; Yan's clan was destroyed and Hushu soon lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興元年正月丙子，司馬元顯將西討桓玄，建牙揚州南門，其東者難立，良久乃正。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day of the first month of the first year of Yuanxing of Emperor An of Jin, Sima Yuanxian was about to march west against Huan Xuan and set up his command pennant at Yangzhou's southern gate; the eastern one was hard to raise and only after long effort stood straight.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the first month of the first year of Yuanxing, Sima Yuanxian marched against Huan Xuan and raised his pennant at Yangzhou's south gate; the eastern staff was hard to set and long in straightening.

sentences.zh: 近沴妖也。

translations.literal: A recent portent of violation.
translations.idiomatic: A recent omen of cosmic violation.

sentences.zh: 尋為桓玄所禽。

translations.literal: Soon he was captured by Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan soon captured him.

sentences.zh: 元興三年五月，樂賢堂壞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanxing, the Hall of Cherishing the Worthy collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanxing the Hall of Cherishing the Worthy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 天意若曰，安帝嚚眊，不及有樂賢之心，故此堂見沴也。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent was as if to say: Emperor An was stupid and dim and did not reach the mind of cherishing the worthy; therefore this hall met violation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven meant: Emperor An was dull and never cherished worthies—so the hall was struck.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙九年五月乙酉，國子聖堂壞。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day of the fifth month of the ninth year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, the Imperial Academy's Hall of the Sage collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the fifth month of the ninth year of Yixi, the Imperial Academy's Hall of the Sage collapsed.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十七年，劉斌為吳郡，郡堂屋西頭鴟尾無故落地，治之未畢，東頭鴟尾復落。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, when Liu Bin was Inspector of Wu commandery, the western owl-tail of the commandery hall fell for no reason; before repairs were finished the eastern owl-tail fell again.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia, while Liu Bin governed Wu, the western owl-tail of the hall fell; before repairs ended the eastern owl-tail fell too.

sentences.zh: 頃之，斌誅。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Bin was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bin was executed.
